name: Kazakhstan
summary: A golden sun with 32 rays above a soaring steppe eagle on a sky-blue field, with a vertical band of national ornament at the hoist. Adopted in 1992, it draws on the symbolism of the Turkic and Mongol peoples of the steppe.
origin: After the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991, Kazakhstan held a competition for new state symbols. The artist Shaken Niyazbekov's design was chosen, and the flag was adopted on 4 June 1992.
The Constitutional Law on State Symbols of 2007 governs its use and specifies its colours.

colors.name: Sky blue
colors.meaning: The endless sky over the steppe; peace, well-being and the unity of the Turkic peoples, for whom blue has religious significance.

colors.name: Gold
colors.meaning: The sun, eagle and ornament; light and wealth.

symbols.name: Sun
symbols.meaning: A source of life and energy; wealth and abundance.

symbols.name: Steppe eagle (berkut)
symbols.description: A golden eagle with spread wings beneath the sun.
symbols.meaning: Freedom, power and the high aspirations of the state.

symbols.name: Koshkar-muiz ornament
symbols.description: A vertical band of traditional 'ram's horn' patterns at the hoist.
symbols.meaning: The art and cultural traditions of the Kazakh people.

history.label: Kazakh SSR
history.note: Red with a horizontal light blue band.

facts: Flag Day, 4 June, is the anniversary of its adoption.
Its sky-blue field is one of the lightest blues among national flags.
clues: A golden sun and eagle on sky blue, with an ornamental band at the hoist.
Its hoist band shows a 'ram's horn' pattern.
Adopted in 1992 after a competition, replacing a Soviet republic flag.
